subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime calls to sessions.create continue to fail closed when the selected parent or existing target is a legacy ownerless session, matching the existing delete boundary?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but this is an intentional compatibility boundary for persisted legacy sessions and needs maintainer ownership rather than inference from unit coverage.

options.title: Accept fail-closed legacy ownership
options.body: Approve rejecting plugin access to ownerless parent and target sessions, then require real loaded-plugin Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve legacy parent access
options.body: Define a narrowly scoped migration or compatibility policy for ownerless rows instead of applying unconditional rejection.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed legacy ownership
recommendation.body: Approve rejecting plugin access to ownerless parent and target sessions, then require real loaded-plugin Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current session RPC ownership boundaries sit in the handler architecture introduced by the gateway session split.
